name: Hard disk drives

comps.spec: Pair of curved neodymium magnets on steel plates — very strong; they pinch skin and chip if they snap together
comps.loc: Under the head arm, held by one or two screws

comps.spec: Mirror-polished platters (aluminium, or glass in many laptop drives) — good signal mirrors
Flat voice coil on the head arm
Logic board with motor driver, processor and cache chip
comps.loc: Underside, held by small Torx screws

notes: Torx T6–T9 bits open most drives; one screw often hides under the label. Desktop (3.5 in) drives have the biggest magnets. External drives add a 12V or 5V adapter and a USB board.

sources.title: Open Repair Alliance, Open Repair Data v0.3 (community repair events, 2012 to July 2026; CC BY-SA 4.0): 479 repairs recorded as PC accessory (hard drive subset)
